headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: AutoGen’s code-executing, file-accessing orchestration can feed Open WebUI’s MCP/tooling and shared files into unsafe cross-agent flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute tool calls/code, while open-webui can ingest files and expose MCP/OpenAPI tools. A shared workspace or tool-output bridge lets attacker-controlled content from one side be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default deployments, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted volume, injected content can cross from one to the other.
IF open-webui MCP or tool output is forwarded into AutoGen prompts, instruction hijacking becomes possible.
mitigations: Separate working directories and mounted volumes.
Disable MCP/tool ingestion for untrusted content.
Add a strict allowlist for files AutoGen may read.
Prefix all cross-agent content as data, not instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and prompt-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and has broad filesystem/network access; open-webui touches files, persistent memory, analytics, and API keys, and can call many external APIs. If they share files or a session-backed workspace, sensitive prompts, documents, or keys can flow into outbound requests or logs. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same mounted files or workspace, sensitive documents may be exposed to both.
IF open-webui is configured with external API/search tools, content from shared files can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared directories.
Use separate service accounts and API keys.
Disable external tools for sensitive sessions.
Restrict file mounts to least-privilege paths.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound tool calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; open-webui can also access local files and mounted volumes, with persistent multi-worker sessions. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared artifacts or state in the same directory, creating race conditions and overwrite risk. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mounted volume, file clobbering can occur.
IF the orchestrator provides no locking, concurrent edits can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Enable per-agent file locks where available.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Use immutable handoff files between agents.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate tool outputs and code-derived claims, while open-webui supports tool calling and can route outputs into downstream actions or chat responses. If open-webui treats AutoGen output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or user-facing misinformation. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards AutoGen output into tools or browser actions without validation, mistakes can propagate.
IF AutoGen emits unverified facts that open-webui renders as trusted answers, downstream users may act on them.
mitigations: Require human review before actions.
Add citation/verification checks on imported outputs.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted by default.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and application data, while open-webui touches prompts, documents, notes, persistent memory, analytics, files, and API keys. If the pair is used on regulated or residency-bound data, their differing storage and outbound-tool patterns can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction conflict, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into both agents, retention and logging differences can create policy violations.
IF open-webui external tools are enabled, residency-bound data may leave the approved boundary.
mitigations: Block regulated data from shared sessions.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Disable analytics and external search for sensitive workloads.
Document data-flow boundaries for operators.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
